newsitem.title: USA: Texas cattle group studies cooperative marketing.
newsitem.headline: Texas cattle group studies cooperative marketing.

text.p: In an attempt to strengthen their marketing positions with meat packers, Texas cattlemen are studying the creation of a cattle marketing cooperative.

Development of such a cooperative is in its infancy, but under such a system, cattle from several member feedlots would be sold by the cooperative rather than by the individual feedyard, said Texas Cattle Feeders Association officials.
"This is the one (marketing plan) we are talking about and working on right now," said TCFA President Randall Graham.

Graham said to be successful, the cooperative would have to control at least 50,000 head of cattle a week. During the TCFA's annual convention under way here, Graham said the cooperative system could assure cattle being sold in "a timely fashion at a fair price."
"You would have market strength through numbers," he said. "We need to have some of that control to market cattle in an orderly manner."

In recent months, meat packers typically have bought large amounts of cattle one day a week rather than spreading purchases out over several days. Graham and others believe a cooperative marketing program would spread out marketings over several days.
Last week for example, meat packers largely stayed out of the market until Thursday at which time they did the bulk of the week's buying.
TCFA has consulted with cattle groups in other states about cooperative marketing programs, but the Texas group is working independently on the project, Graham said.
